newsitem.title: USA: Most emerging debt follows U.S. Treasuries higher.
newsitem.headline: Most emerging debt follows U.S. Treasuries higher.

text.p: Most emerging market debt rose as U.S. Treasuries yields again declined and Brazil completed another leg of its cellular telephone service privatization, Brady bond traders said.
"I think the market is staying up here and moving higher because of the Treasury market more than anything else," one trader said.
After Brazil awarded a 20-year concession to run B Band cellular service in Sao Paolo, Brazil C bonds rose 3/8 to 83-3/8 and the global '27 rose 3/4 to 99-3/8.
The BCP consortium led by BellSouth Corp and Banco Safra placed the winning bid of 2.65 billion reais, more than four times higher than the 600 million real minimum price.
"Basically it was because of the selling of the cellular services" that Brazil debt rose, a head Brady trader said.

Other countries' debt instruments turned in a more mixed performance. Argentina FRBs slipped 1/8 to 94-7/8 during a market holiday in the nation, and Mexico pars dipped 1/4 to 80-1/4 amid some profit-taking, traders said.
"Besides Brazil, there is very little customer flow," one trader said.

Peru FLIRBs rose 1/8 to 60-7/8 after Finance Minister Jorge Camet, speaking in New York, said Peru would use fresh bond issues rather than relying on its fiscal surplus if it decided to repurchase existing foreign debt.
In an interview with Reuters Financial Television, Camet added that Peru had studied the possibility of repurchasing its Brady bonds but had not yet come to a decision.
Traders said the comments had little impact on prices.
